subject: Consolidated OKR Scores + QBR narrative: actionable summaries
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: jenna.rogers@acme-analytics.com, tom.alvarez@datapulse.io
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Consolidated OKR Scores + QBR narrative: actionable summaries

Team — attaching the consolidated scoring workbook and a first-pass narrative for the QBR slides. This is focused on the end-of-quarter judgments we need for the exec bundle and the customer-facing QBR for Acme.

Top-level asks:
- Please review the scoring column (sheet: "final_scores") and call out any objections or evidence that would change a numerical judgment by EOD Wed (Feb 17).
- For any objective where you propose a change, add a 1–2 line rationale in the "rationale" column and keep the evidence pointer (drive/notion link) updated.
- We need one concise customer-facing sentence per objective for the QBR slide (see tab "one-liners").

Notes / areas I flagged:
- Reliability: raised from 3 -> 2 in the draft because of the two incidents in Jan; Laura, this is probably where you and infra will have the strongest pushback.
- Cost per token: improving but still behind target; we include planned Optimize rollout in the narrative as a forward-looking item.
- GTM/ARR motions: strong performance vs plan; recommend we mark as achieved but include clarifying note about pipeline seasonality.

Attachments referenced: Q1_OKR_Scoring_v3.xlsx (latest); QBR_Slides_Draft_v1.pdf.

I'll iterate and publish the final slides to Drive once you sign off. Jenna/Tom — I've cc'd you for transparency; if you'd like any changes to the customer-facing language, flag them and we'll accommodate.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Sales & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Consolidated OKR Scores + QBR narrative: actionable summaries

Karthik — quick inline on Reliability:

On Mon, Feb 15, 2027 at 9:12 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — attaching the consolidated scoring workbook and a first-pass narrative for the QBR slides.
> 
> Notes / areas I flagged:
> - Reliability: raised from 3 -> 2 in the draft because of the two incidents in Jan; Laura, this is probably where you and infra will have the strongest pushback.

I pushed a comment in the sheet with the incident postmortem links. My position: keep Reliability at 3 (partial success) rather than 2. Rationale: SEV incidents were contained, customer impact limited to <2% of requests, and the runbook updates are already validated in staging. If we mark it as 2 we need to explicitly commit to the mitigation timeline in the narrative — otherwise it reads like regression.

Suggested one-liner for customer slide: "Improved platform stability; incidents were limited and mitigations validated, with planned follow-up to reduce recurrence risk."

Also: please remove the line in the deck that projects a mid-Q2 feature release date for Optimize; that date is optimistic. We should phrase as "planned H2 rollout" unless engineering confirms.

—Laura
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
[attachment: incident_postmortem_Jan_incidents.docx]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Consolidated OKR Scores + QBR narrative: actionable summaries

Thanks — high level framing suggestion: for the exec slides I want us to present three signals per objective: (1) outcome metric (score), (2) supporting evidence (1 line), (3) forward ask/next milestone. That keeps the QBR crisp for execs and partners.

On the Reliability judgment: I agree with Laura's reasoning. Karthik, please accept her change in the workbook and add the mitigation timeline (date-based) under "next milestone" — execs need a commitment item.

Marissa — can you take the one-liners and convert them to the slide language? Keep them customer-facing and avoid implementation details. Jenna/Tom: if you have any edits to customer-safety phrasing, flag them directly in the deck comments.

Vivek
Chief Product Officer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Consolidated OKR Scores + QBR narrative: actionable summaries

Attached: Q1_OKR_Scoring_v4.xlsx — I accepted Laura's reliability note, adjusted the Cost per Token narrative to reflect an interim 8% improvement (vs the 12% target), and added a short evidence pointer for GTM motion conversions into the notes column.

Changes summary (in the sheet):
- Reliability: score left at 3, mitigation timeline added (target: complete by 2027-03-15).
- Cost per token: score remains 3; evidence links added to Optimize pilot dashboard.
- GTM ARR: score 4; clarified that expansion ARR includes two large renewals expected in Q2.

Attachments: Q1_OKR_Scoring_v4.xlsx (spreadsheet), scoring_rationale_notes.docx (detailed comments).

Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Folks — thanks for the quick turn. I've pulled Marissa's sheet into the deck and drafted the exec narrative in the Notion doc (link below). Highlights:

- Final judgments reflected in attached Q1_OKR_Scoring_v4.xlsx.
- Slide 2: executive summary with three-signal format (score / evidence / next milestone).
- Slide 6: customer-facing talking points for Acme; Jenna — I've tried to keep it direct and non-technical.

Please do two final things by EOD Thurs:
1) Approve the deck if you have no substantive edits. A one-line reply here that says "approve" is fine.
2) If you request edits, add them as comments in the Drive file or reply with the exact copy change.

Notion narrative: https://www.notion.so/redwood/OKR-QBR-Storyline-9f7a

Thanks,
Karthik
